projects.title: Selected Work
projects.intro: Web products built around sales, trust, admin control, and real business use after launch.

laibi.title: Supermarket Laibi 2
laibi.shortDescription: A supermarket ordering web app built to work like a mobile app without native app cost.
laibi.value: It gave the owner admin control over products, stock, categories, images, and orders. Reported sales increased by 130% on average.

images.cardAlt: Supermarket Laibi 2 web app project card

lead.title: Sell online without paying for native apps
lead.body: The supermarket needed a cheaper digital ordering channel that still felt easy on phones.

problem.title: Orders were hard to manage manually
problem.body: The owner needed less phone chaos, clearer product updates, and a faster way to receive customer orders.

system.title: Catalog, cart, and admin panel
system.body: Products, stock, categories, images, cart logic, and order tracking all live in one controlled system.

outcome.title: More orders with less admin work
outcome.body: The app became the main digital sales surface and made daily store updates easier to manage.

rimoochat.title: Rimoochat
rimoochat.shortDescription: A handmade clothing store built around trust, rarity, and a clear buying path.
rimoochat.value: The store helped the family business turn online attention into sales. It now drives more than 90% of current income.

lead.title: Make handmade clothes feel worth buying
lead.body: The store needed to show care, rarity, and trust fast for mothers buying clothes for their kids.

problem.title: A normal catalog would make it feel cheap
problem.body: The products needed a soft story and a direct path to purchase, not a generic product grid.

system.title: Storefront shaped around one audience
system.body: The layout, copy, product framing, and mobile flow all support a focused customer group.

outcome.title: The store became the main income channel
outcome.body: The family now relies on the website as the main place where customers browse and buy.

unimarket.title: Unimarket
unimarket.shortDescription: A student marketplace built for USTHB buyers and sellers instead of generic selling channels.
unimarket.value: It added trust with auth, email verification, moderation, seller flows, buyer flows, and local payment logic.

lead.title: Create a trusted student marketplace
lead.body: USTHB students needed one focused place to sell, buy, and trade inside their own university environment.

problem.title: Generic platforms had weak trust
problem.body: Students had no dedicated seller flow, no campus-focused browsing, and no moderation layer.

system.title: Marketplace logic from zero
system.body: Auth, email verification, buyer flow, seller flow, listings, moderation, and cash-on-delivery handling.

outcome.title: A real marketplace system
outcome.body: The platform replaced scattered selling with a cleaner, safer, and more focused student trade experience.

howIWork.title: How I work
howIWork.intro: A useful project starts with the business case: who needs it, what should become easier, where the value is, and what counts as a win.

discovery.label: Discovery call
discovery.value: Project context, target users, current workflow, risks, and success metrics get mapped first.

mvp.label: MVP shape
mvp.value: The first working version is defined clearly. Nice-to-have features wait.

agreement.label: Agreement
agreement.value: Scope, investment, timeline, milestones, and responsibilities are written before build starts.

chat.clientStart: Hey Heithem. I want to launch a store, startup, or web app. What should be clear before we start?
chat.heithemIntro: Happy to help. Send the rough version first: what the product should do, who will use it, and where it should make money or save time.
chat.heithemCall: A free 30-minute voice or video call is usually enough to map the idea, the risks, the first version, and the success metric.
chat.clientInvestment: Good. What kind of investment should I expect for the web app?
chat.heithemInvestment: The investment becomes clear after discovery. It depends on scope, complexity, timeline, integrations, and what the first version needs to prove.
chat.heithemRange: For a working online store with the important parts included, investment usually starts around $1.5k to $3k. Complex platforms need discovery first, then a clean number.
chat.clientCall: Makes sense. Let’s start with the call.
chat.callNote: Discovery call: project goal, users, MVP scope, risks, timeline, and success metrics.
chat.heithemAgreement: Next comes a short agreement: scope, investment, timeline, milestones, what is included, and what is needed from your side.
chat.heithemClose: Perfect. Once you give the OK on the agreement, work starts.

about.title: Web apps that move the business.

paragraphs.one: Specialized in building web apps using software engineering knowledge, turning complex business problems into clean, functional systems.
paragraphs.two: The work fits stores, startups, dashboards, and platforms where the app needs to handle real logic, not only look good on the first screen.
paragraphs.three: The goal is simple: create a product that helps sell, manage, decide, or save time through something people can use every day.

about.centerBody: Working for 2 startups as their tech co-founder and decision maker on the tech side of the work.

one.title: Experience aimed at business value.
one.text: With 5 years in engineering and 2 years developing web apps for startups and business owners, the focus is on targeted products designed to bring value to the investor based on the project’s real needs.

two.title: The client’s field becomes part of the app.
two.text: The best web apps feel specific. The client’s experience in the field becomes part of the product, then gets shaped into clean UI, strong speed, secure logic, and a web app that brings more value to the table.
